name: Health Insurance and AI
blurb: Where AI decides what a health plan will pay for. Prior authorization algorithms under the CMS rules, claims adjudication and batch denials, the Medicare Advantage denial lawsuits against UnitedHealth, Cigna and Humana, state utilization review laws such as California's Physicians Make Decisions Act, underwriting and pricing with AI, fraud detection, health data privacy in insurer models, the insurer's own liability, the provider's side, and the Medicare and marketplace rules.

points.desc: Software that scores a request against coverage criteria before a plan will pay, in Medicare Advantage, marketplace and commercial plans, and the federal rules that now limit it.
points.name: Prior authorization algorithms

points.desc: Post-service claim review by algorithm, where a system flags claims as not matching a diagnosis or coverage rule and a reviewer signs off on many at once.
points.name: Claims adjudication and batch denials

points.desc: The class actions over nH Predict and similar tools used to cut off post-acute and rehabilitation care for Medicare Advantage members, now on this site's tracker.
points.name: The Medicare Advantage denial lawsuits

points.desc: State laws that say who may make a medical necessity decision, and the new ones written specifically about algorithms.
points.name: State utilization review laws

points.desc: What an insurer may use to price or accept a risk when the model can infer far more than the application asks.
points.name: Underwriting and pricing with AI

points.desc: Machine learning that flags providers, claims and patterns for review, run by CMS, by plans and by their vendors.
points.name: Fraud, waste and abuse detection

points.desc: What an insurer's model may learn from, and the HIPAA rules that follow the data into the vendor's system.
points.name: Health data privacy in insurer AI

points.desc: When an algorithm denies care, the claims that follow: bad faith, breach of contract, unfair business practice, and the errors and omissions and D&O exposure behind them.
points.name: Liability for the insurer

points.desc: Practices and hospitals answering algorithmic denials with their own automation, and the documentation that survives a model's review.
points.name: The provider's side

points.desc: The two programs where federal rules on AI coverage decisions are most developed, each with its own page on this site.
points.name: Medicare and the marketplace
